```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(knbsdata)
```

County-level work in Kenya lives or dies on join keys. This vignette covers
the reference codes `knbs_geographies()` provides, the two mistakes that
silently corrupt county joins, and what this package deliberately does not
offer.

Chunks that contact the service are shown but not run.

## The reference

```{r, eval = FALSE}
geo <- knbs_geographies()
counties <- knbs_geographies(level = "county")
mombasa_subs <- knbs_geographies(parent = "01")
```

One row per territorial unit of the 2019 Population and Housing Census frame:
Kenya (`"00"`), 47 counties (`"01"`–`"47"`), and their sub-counties (four
digits, the first two being the county). Names, levels and parent codes come
with it, read live from the census service (CC BY 4.0) rather than shipped as
a snapshot that could drift from the source.

## The two classic corruptions

**Leading zeros.** County codes are character, and `"01"` is not `1`. The
moment a code passes through `as.numeric()` — or through a CSV round-trip
that guesses types — Mombasa (`"01"`) collides with nothing and matches
nothing. Everything in this package keeps codes as character; keep them that
way in your own pipelines, and if you read codes from a file, read that
column as character explicitly.

**Vintage mixing.** These are the *2019 census frame* units. Administrative
units change: joining 2019 codes against a table coded to another frame will
drop or misassign rows without erroring. The `vintage` column exists so that
the frame travels with the data; check it before joining anything that did
not come from this package.

## A worked join

County population against the reference, giving each county its share:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
pop <- knbs_get_indicator("POPCEN0001", geo_level = "county")
totals <- pop[pop$sex == "total" & pop$p18_vs1 == "T",
              c("geo_code", "geo_name", "value")]

geo <- knbs_geographies(level = "county")
joined <- merge(totals, geo[, c("geo_code", "parent_code")], by = "geo_code")

joined$share <- joined$value / sum(joined$value)
head(joined[order(-joined$share), ])
```

The join is exact by construction: observations and reference use the same
codes from the same source.

## Gross County Product

The county economy itself is served by the Open Data for Africa republisher
(`source_id` `"opendataforafrica"`), the one source that carries GCP as
data: GVA shares plus constant- and current-price GCP for all 47 counties,
annual 2013–2020.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
gcp <- knbs_get_indicator("jhbzkjc")
latest <- gcp[gcp$table == "T3" & gcp$period == 2020 & gcp$geo_code != "KE", ]
head(latest[order(-latest$value), c("geo_name", "value")])
```

Two cautions, both stated in `knbs_metadata()`: this is the **2021 edition**
— newer GCP years exist only as PDF reports
(`knbs_publications("gross county product")`) — and its geography codes are
the **portal's own region codes**, not census territories. To relate GCP to
census-coded data, join **by county name**, deliberately and visibly, not by
code.

## What is deliberately absent

- **Other vintages and crosswalks.** Only the 2019 frame has a verified
  source. `knbs_geographies(vintage = 2009)` fails with a clear error rather
  than serving an unverified concordance — a wrong crosswalk is worse than
  none.
- **Boundaries.** `knbs_boundaries()` does not exist. No officially licensed,
  redistributable boundary file has been verified, and the plan implements
  boundaries only after that review.
- **Classifications.** Industry, occupation and product classifications have
  no audited source yet.

If you know an official source for any of these, a
[data source change issue](https://github.com/Mustapha-Wasseja/knbsdata/issues/new/choose)
is the right place to point at it.
